When the world's largest crypto exchange can be hit by a multi billion dollar hack and still promise to plug the hole, one thing jumps out: investors are relying heavily on leadership they trust. That is the opening for backing founders who built their businesses and still steer them today. This article breaks down three such founder run stocks and why they deserve a closer look now.

The three stocks highlighted here offer a compelling starting point if you want exposure to founder led businesses where leadership is personally invested in building long term legacies. However, if you want the absolute best, these 28 top founder-led companies are the cream of the crop.

Meta Platforms (META)

Overview: Meta Platforms runs Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger and related AI and VR products, with founder Mark Zuckerberg still directly steering major decisions.

Operations: Meta generates about US$239.4b from its Family of Apps segment and US$2.2b from Reality Labs, with additional multinational revenue diversification.

Market Cap: US$1.60t

Meta Platforms fits the Founder Led Companies theme because Zuckerberg is not just a figurehead. He is actively redirecting a huge social media empire toward ambitious AI and immersive tech bets that few non founder CEOs would dare to underwrite.

"Reality Labs lost $19.19 billion in 2025. Nineteen billion dollars. Roughly the GDP of Iceland, spent annually with no prospect of near-term return."

What really matters now is how one unresolved pressure on Meta's future cash generation shapes the payoff from that founder driven ambition.

That unresolved pressure is exactly what the full narrative for Meta Platforms unpacks, showing how Meta Platforms could turn heavy Reality Labs spending into an accelerating edge if the thesis plays out.

Cerebras Systems (CBRS)

Overview: Cerebras Systems builds wafer-scale AI chips and rack-scale compute platforms under founder Andrew Feldman's direct product and go to market leadership.

Operations: Cerebras generates US$680.7 million from semiconductors, with US$236.6 million from the United States and US$443.5 million from Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.

Market Cap: US$27.3b

Cerebras Systems matters for a founder led approach because the same engineers who reimagined the hardware are still personally steering how it is deployed at scale.

"In March 2026, AWS integrated Cerebras CS-3 systems directly into Amazon Bedrock, splitting inference between Trainium3 for the prefill phase and the Cerebras wafer for decode, yielding up to a 15x speed improvement over monolithic GPU setups."

Meta (META) Stock Sees Modest Fair Value Lift As Muse And Financing Drive Debate
Bailey Pemberton

META
TFC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The fair value estimate for Meta Platforms has been updated from US$813.65 to US$848.38 per share, giving you a fresh reference point against a busy period of news and debate around the stock. This shift comes as analysts focus on the Muse product ramp, the US$95b equity financing, and what these developments could mean for how the market frames upside and risk. As you read on, you will see how to track these moving parts and keep up with the evolving Meta Platforms story.

Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value Meta Platforms.

What Wall Street Has Been Saying
🐂 Bullish Takeaways

Several firms have raised valuation ranges on Meta Platforms following Q3 results and the Muse launch. Examples include Truist lifting its target to US$1,000, Wells Fargo to US$1,000, Tigress Financial to US$995, and Pivotal Research to US$960, reflecting updated long term cash flow and AI product assumptions.

JPMorgan, Citi, BofA, Deutsche Bank and others highlight strong core advertising performance, with firms like Evercore ISI and RBC Capital pointing to Q3 revenue and engagement metrics that support their higher targets between roughly US$800 and US$900.

Muse is a key driver of the current Meta Platforms investment debate. Barclays, TD Cowen, Jefferies and Deutsche Bank describe early user traction and engagement as strong, and see potential for new revenue streams across agents, business messaging and hardware integration.

Multiple firms, including Cantor Fitzgerald, KeyBanc, Citizens and Raymond James, argue that Meta Platforms now has several AI related product paths that could support growth beyond the existing ad business over time.

🐻 Bearish Takeaways

Oppenheimer and Wedbush flag concerns that Muse monetization may take time and that usage and password trust could limit willingness to pay, which keeps them cautious on the size and timing of any financial impact.

Goldman Sachs and Oppenheimer highlight debate around higher 2027 operating expenses and capital expenditures linked to AI and Muse, along with the need for external funding. The US$95b equity plan discussed by Mizuho and Piper Sandler also brings dilution into focus even if some interest expense could be reduced.

META
GOOG
AMZN
ORCL

Trading disclosure

Hyperscalers are currently offering bond yields between 6% and 8%, drawing investor attention away from volatile equities.

Tech giants are grappling with unprecedented capital expenditures and negative free cash flows, with cumulative debt and equity issuance hitting $271 billion this year.

Recent equity maneuvers—such as Meta's $95 billion stock offering plan—signal that the historic era of aggressive corporate stock buybacks may be coming to a close.

Bank of America guided investors toward mega-cap technology corporate bonds instead of equities as an investment opportunity. Michael Hartnett, chief investment strategist at BofA, noted that fixed-income instruments issued by the "Magnificent Seven" and other major tech players provide compelling value.

The surge in borrowing costs stems directly from escalating anxiety surrounding the massive capital expenditures made by hyperscalers like Meta (META), Google (GOOG, GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), and Oracle (ORCL), among others, to build out generative artificial intelligence infrastructure.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

As tech firms tap capital markets aggressively to fund these heavy digital expansions, BofA highlighted that the yields on investment-grade debt have climbed to attractive ranges between 6% and 8%.

Soaring Capex And Earnings Pressure

The pivot toward debt markets comes on the heels of a turbulent week for technology stocks. Following quarterly earnings reports, several major tech corporations revealed unexpectedly high negative free cash flows alongside staggering capital expenditures.

Industry giants continue to scale up investments exponentially, pushing projected annual capital expenditures higher. For instance, Google's 2026 AI capex is expected to land in the $195 billion to $205 billion range. Even traditional holdouts are altering their financing strategies; Microsoft recently announced a $25 billion debt issuance to support its artificial intelligence initiatives. Across the sector, total debt and equity issuance by major hyperscalers has reached $271 billion for the year.

Implications For Shareholders

While the debt market offers high yields—with Oracle leading investment-grade tech bonds above 8% and companies like Meta and Amazon offering yields between 6.8% and 7.4%—the equity landscape faces fresh headwinds.

Meta Platforms recently bucked the pure-debt trend by turning to equity financing, announcing plans to secure $95 billion via stock offerings.

title: Amazon (AMZN) Stock After Q3 Earnings: Buy the Dip, Sell, or Hold?
detail:
Amazon (AMZN) Stock After Q3 Earnings: Buy the Dip, Sell, or Hold?
Shaun Pruitt
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:23 PM EDT 3 min read
AMZN
GOOG
NVDA
META
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Amazon AMZN) stock is under pressure following the e-commerce and cloud computing giant's third-quarter earnings release on Thursday evening, which fell short of Wall Street's top-and bottom-line expectations.

Like Alphabet GOOGL), Amazon disappointed investors as concerns about massive artificial intelligence spending overshadowed otherwise encouraging growth. However, AMZN's post-earnings selloff has been less severe than Alphabet's, with Amazon shares falling roughly 7% in Friday's premarket trading.

Still, Amazon's accelerating AWS growth, expanding AI opportunities, and improving operating profitability raise the question of whether the pullback presents a buying opportunity.

Amazon's Q3 Results: Earnings Miss, but Record Margins

Amazon reported Q3 earnings of $1.89 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.01 and declining from EPS of $1.95 in the year-ago quarter.

Revenue climbed 12% year over year to $201.94 billion but narrowly missed expectations of $202.11 billion.

Encouragingly, operating income surged 61% to $28.1 billion, with Amazon achieving a record operating margin of 13.9%, highlighting improving profitability across its businesses despite substantial AI investments.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AWS Growth Accelerates as AI Spending Surges

Amazon Web Services (AWS) remained a standout performer, with Q3 revenue soaring 39% YoY to $46 billion, marking its fastest growth in nearly five years. AWS operating income also jumped 55% to $17.8 billion.

Growth is being fueled by surging demand for AI infrastructure and cloud computing, including Amazon's custom Trainium AI chips and Bedrock generative AI platform. New AWS agreements with major technology companies, including OpenAI, Meta Platforms META), and Nvidia NVDA), further highlight Amazon's expanding AI ecosystem.

CEO Andy Jassy projected AWS revenue growth exceeding 40% in both 2027 and 2028, reinforcing confidence in Amazon's long-term cloud and AI opportunities.

However, Amazon reaffirmed its massive $220 billion capital expenditure outlook for 2026, primarily reflecting AI infrastructure investments. The spending has pressured free cash flow, with Amazon joining Alphabet in posting negative free cash flow in Q3.

Amazon's quarterly free cash flow was negative $33.5 billion, bringing its trailing 12-month cash outflow to $42.4 billion, compared with positive free cash flow of $14.8 billion over the prior 12-month period.

Amazon's Q4 Guidance: Holiday Growth Ahead

Looking ahead, Amazon expects Q4 revenue of $240-$247 billion, representing 12%-16% YoY growth as the holiday shopping season approaches and coming in range of Wall Street's forecast of $245.65 billion (Current Qtr below).
